Performing the operation will never increase mex\operatorname{mex}, so we perform mm operations.
Next, we consider computing the maximum value of f⁡(a)f(a). First, we have f⁡(a)≤n−m⋅kf(a)\leq n-m\cdot k because after the operations, the length of aa becomes n−m⋅kn-m\cdot k, and the mex\operatorname{mex} of a sequence must be no more than its length. Second, we have f⁡(a)≤nm+1f(a)\leq\frac{n}{m+1}, because to ensure that all numbers in 0∼f⁡(a)−10\sim f(a)-1 are not completely removed, each of them must appear at least m+1m+1 times.
Now, we claim that the maximum value of f⁡(a)f(a) is min⁡(n−m⋅k,⌊nm+1⌋)\min(n-m\cdot k,\left\lfloor\frac{n}{m+1}\right\rfloor).
Next, we prove that this maximum can be achieved through construction. If n−m⋅k<nm+1n-m\cdot k<\frac{n}{m+1}, then n<(m+1)⋅kn<(m+1)\cdot k, which implies n−m⋅k<kn-m\cdot k<k, meaning that the final length of aa is less than kk. In this case, we construct ai=imodka_{i}=i\bmod k. This ensures that no matter which subarray is removed, the remaining sequence still satisfies ai=imodka_{i}=i\bmod k. After performing mm deletions, we are left with ai=ia_{i}=i. If n−m⋅k≥nm+1n-m\cdot k\geq\frac{n}{m+1}, then n≥(m+1)⋅kn\geq(m+1)\cdot k, which implies nm+1≥k\frac{n}{m+1}\geq k. Here, we construct ai=imod⌈nm+1⌉a_{i}=i\bmod\left\lceil\frac{n}{m+1}\right\rceil. This guarantees that every pair of identical numbers has a distance of at least kk, and that all numbers in 0∼⌈nm+1⌉−10\sim\left\lceil\frac{n}{m+1}\right\rceil-1 appear at least m+1m+1 times. Thus, each deletion can remove at most one of these numbers, ensuring that no number is completely removed after mm deletions.
